source.title: Making Coherence Out of Nothing At All: Measuring the Evolution of Gradient Alignment

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures gradient coherence during training with randomized labels and reports that training reaches only about 80% accuracy in the 100% noise setting, qualifying the claim that these networks fit random labels to near-zero error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training and test accuracy in Figure 1, but most accuracy values are figure-only. Its coherence measurements are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions’ named outcomes. The authors note that training with random labels continued only until about 80% accuracy was reached.
record.test_reason: The study trains standard networks with SGD on randomized labels and reports training accuracy, directly bearing on V1 and V4. Its approximately 80% endpoint reflects a stopped run, not demonstrated inability to reach zero error; T5 is therefore inappropriate.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that SGD creates gradient coherence even with random labels, suggesting an optimization phenomenon. They argue that CG needs an additional theory explaining coherence creation; they do not conclude that random labels cannot be fitted perfectly.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies ImageNet label-noise variants and gradient coherence over training, rather than reproducing the original studies’ memorization experiments. It uses ResNet-18, SGD with momentum, batch size 4096, and turns off augmentation and weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the rate of coherence increase depends inversely on the amount of label noise; it also reports different coherence values across layers and architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient coherence increases even with fully random labels, reaching hundreds of mutually supporting examples; its growth is slower with more label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD creates per-example gradient alignment during memorization, with label noise affecting the rate of coherence growth.

fits_no_version.finding: Real-label and random-label coherence follow broadly similar rising and falling trajectories on different timescales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-alignment dynamics share a broad trajectory across real and randomized labels.

record.problems: The random-label training run did not continue to zero error; it reached only about 80% accuracy. Most training and test accuracy results are shown only in figures, without precise text values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying accuracy results were extracted: other noise-condition accuracies appear only in figures without textual descriptions sufficient to place their values.

untested.parts: Eventual near-zero training error after the random-label run was stopped, and a readable numerical demonstration of chance-level test accuracy.
Training time to matched fitting thresholds and its ratio between true and random labels. Coherence growth rates do not measure convergence time.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Eventual perfect fit beyond the observed random-label endpoint. The supplied text does not resolve whether test error rises steadily across noise fractions.
Controlled effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization. Disabling regularization throughout supplies no comparison.
Direct measurements separating the learning of shared real patterns from subsequent memorization of noisy examples.

missing.what: Inception-V3 training and test accuracy results for 0%, 50%, and 100% randomized labels are shown but have no rows. Their values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text extraction.

record.verdict_notes: The introduction's near-100% random-label accuracy statement summarizes prior work, not this study's endpoint. No challenges verdict is warranted from an intentionally stopped run. Accuracy curves are not recoverable from the supplied figure text; no numerical values were inferred from axes. The 25% and 75% accuracy conditions are already covered by rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests random labels with ResNet-18 under its stated ImageNet setup; it does not test other architectures or the claim’s full range of training hyperparameters.
The paper tests several label-noise fractions, but does not textually report a steady rise in test error toward chance or perfect training fit across the full sweep.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ImageNet with all training labels randomized; SGD with momentum (0.9), batch size 4096, stated learning-rate schedule; weight decay and augmentation turned off.
rows.note: The authors say training continued only until about 80% accuracy was reached, so this setting did not demonstrate near-zero training error.
rows.check: The approximately 80% training accuracy is correctly extracted, but training stopped there. It establishes substantial, incomplete memorization within the observed run, not failed convergence or a ceiling on achievable accuracy. Weight decay and augmentation were disabled for all noise conditions.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ImageNet with original labels; SGD with momentum (0.9), batch size 4096, stated learning-rate schedule; weight decay and augmentation turned off.
rows.note: The text gives no precise training or test accuracy result for this condition.
rows.check: The text explicitly states that all real-label training examples were fitted, so training fit is not wholly figure-only. Test accuracy remains unreadable from the supplied figure extraction. Split training and test accuracy into separate rows; this clean-label endpoint alone cannot establish the noise-dependent trend.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ImageNet with half the training labels randomized; SGD with momentum (0.9), batch size 4096, stated learning-rate schedule; weight decay and augmentation turned off.
rows.note: The text describes the dataset condition but gives no precise training or test accuracy result for it.
rows.check: The supplied figure extraction does not preserve readable accuracy curves. Split training and test accuracy into separate rows; neither endpoint nor the cross-condition test-error trend can be established from axis labels.

relationships.reason: R1 shows substantial but incomplete fitting at approximately 80% training accuracy; the authors stopped training there, so this qualifies demonstrated fit within that run without challenging eventual convergence.
relationships.display_finding: Training stopped at approximately 80% training accuracy, leaving eventual convergence untested.

tranche.reason: The fitting assay trains a standard network on randomized labels with SGD and measures training accuracy. The additional gradient-coherence analysis does not replace that direct test.

source_check.notes: Augmentation and weight decay were disabled for these experiments. The introduction's near-100% fitting discussion describes prior findings; this study's fully randomized run ends near 80%.

statements.correction: ImageNet ResNet-18; fully randomized training labels; approximately 80% training accuracy before training stops; limits_scope for the observed run; eventual perfect fitting untested.
statements.problem: The ImageNet endpoint is correct, but its placement under challenges overstates the evidence: fitting is substantial and incomplete when training stops, rather than absent or reversed.
